newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends strong, Brent rally breaks $20.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends strong, Brent rally breaks $20.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed sharply firmer on Friday, drawing strength from NYMEX heating oil which helped the whole complex reverse earlier losses, brokers said.
March gas oil ended $4.25 up at $169 a tonne. April Brent was trading 30 cents higher at $20.00 a barrel at 1752 GMT, having briefly breached this key resistance level to touch $20.02.
The April Brent/gas oil spread was trading close to $2.90 a barrel, which dealers said was untenable in the longer term.
"I'm surprised gas oil closed as strong as it did, the crack is too wide to feel comfortable," said one dealer.
Despite weak long-term fundamentals, an expected drop in temperatures in the U.S. Northeast -- the world's key heating oil market -- was serving as a short-term prop to the oil complex.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said temperatures in the region would average five degrees Fahrenheit below normal on Friday and remain low throughout the weekend.
"If the strength was coming from gasoline rather than heat we'd be a bit more bullish," said one trader.
The longer-term outlook was more bearish, analysts said.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) said one Friday that OPEC output in February was unchanged from January at 26.98 million barrels per day.

It also said that oil inventories in the world's leading industrial nations recovered in January and ended the month higher than the year before in the first time in January to end the month higher than a year before for the first time in 18 months.

"Most background fundamentals remain essentially unchanged and on the weak side," London brokers GNI said in a daily report. "OPEC production is bearish and high at just under the psychological 27 million barrels per day, and will exceed it before long."
